historical_references.reference: Jiyarul, a legendary king of the Chalukya Dynasty, is said to have ruled from the fortress of Vijayagiri in present-day Badami, Karnataka, India, around the 6th century CE. He is believed to have expanded the Chalukya Empire's territories and is known for his patronage of the arts and architecture.

Another reference to Jiyarul can be found in the 12th-century Sanskrit poem 'Veera Raghavam' by Allasani Peddana. In this work, Jiyarul is mentioned as a great warrior and a devotee of Lord Rama. He is said to have performed a grand 'Ramayana' recitation and palace festival in honor of Lord Rama.
